title: 2000 AMC 12 22
statement: The graph below shows a portion of the curve defined by the quartic polynomial \[P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d.\] Which of the following is the smallest?

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: The product of the zeros of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: The product of the non-real zeros of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: The sum of the coefficients of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: The sum of the real zeros of \(P\)

solutions.text:
The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis exactly twice, both times at positive values, so \(P\) has two real zeros and two non-real (complex conjugate) zeros.

Reading off the graph: the sum of the coefficients is \(P(1) \gt 3;\) \(P(-1) \gt 4;\) the sum of the real zeros is greater than \(4.5;\) and the product of all zeros is \(d,\) the \(y\)-intercept, which is less than \(6.\)

Let \(R\) be the product of the real zeros, so \(R \gt 4.5.\) The product of the non-real zeros is \(\dfrac dR,\) which is less than \(\dfrac{6}{4.5} \lt 2.\)

This is smaller than every other listed quantity.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The graph shows exactly two real zeros, both positive, so \(P\) has two non-real (conjugate) zeros
The product of all zeros equals \(d,\) the \(y\)-intercept; divide it by the product of the real zeros
